links.outcome: Error scores of GPT-4 versus blinded medical experts on the same patient records
links.effect: Overall error scores were comparable between experts and GPT-4 (p=0.301). Experts had fewer missing medications (p=0.008), and GPT-4 had fewer unnecessary medications (p=0.003).
links.quote: The overall error scores were comparable between human experts and GPT-4 (p=0.301).

links.outcome: Completeness of GPT-4 management plans versus ADA guideline reference plan (missing medications)
links.effect: Medical experts' plans had fewer missing medications than GPT-4's (p=0.008). Safety issues appeared in 16% of GPT-4 plans.
links.quote: Safety issues were noted in 16% of the plans generated by GPT-4, highlighting potential risks associated with AI-generated management plans.

links.outcome: Drug dosage accuracy of GPT-4 plans versus expert plans
links.effect: No significant difference in dosage accuracy between GPT-4 and medical experts (p=0.975).
links.quote: No significant difference was observed in the accuracy of drug dosages (p=0.975).

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the safety, completeness, and accuracy of GPT-4 in generating type 2 diabetes management plans using retrospective patient records compared with medical experts, but it does not test a specific deployment safeguard or practice.
